questions.stem: Excessive exposure to microwaves is dangerous because microwaves:

options.explanation: Surface burns are the infrared hazard.
Blindness is the ultraviolet hazard.
Microwaves deposit energy as internal heating of tissue.
That is the gamma and x-ray hazard.
Infrared over-exposure burns the skin.
Radio is the low-energy communications band.
X-ray hazard is cell damage and cancer risk.
Microwaves heat tissue internally rather than browning skin.

questions.stem: Ultraviolet over-exposure can damage surface cells and also cause:

options.explanation: Internal heating is the microwave hazard.
Ultraviolet damages the eyes as well as skin cells.
That is not a listed ultraviolet effect.
That is irrelevant to the human-body harm list.

questions.stem: Gamma rays and x-rays are hazardous because they can:

options.explanation: Gentle heating is a mild effect far below their real hazard.
The hazard list is about the human body.
Sunburn is the ultraviolet effect.

options.text: kill cells, causing cancer and mutation
options.explanation: Cell death from these ionising radiations leads to cancer and mutation risks.

questions.stem: The harm from ultraviolet, gamma and x-ray exposure increases with frequency because:

options.explanation: All EM waves share one speed in free space.

options.text: higher-frequency waves carry more energy and can ionise atoms
options.explanation: Energy rises with frequency, and ionisation begins beyond visible.
Loudness is a sound property, irrelevant here.

options.text: lower-frequency waves are blocked by air
options.explanation: The trend runs with frequency, not with air blocking.

questions.stem: State the harm caused by excessive exposure to infrared radiation.
State two protective measures against ultraviolet exposure.
questions.modelAnswer: Wear sunglasses that absorb ultraviolet, and apply sunscreen that absorbs ultraviolet before it damages the skin.

questions.stem: Explain why radiographers leave the room during x-ray imaging and wear radiation badges.
questions.modelAnswer: X-rays are ionising, so repeated daily exposure would raise their cumulative dose and cancer risk; leaving the room avoids unnecessary exposure and the badge measures the dose they do receive so it can be checked and limited.

questions.stem: A microwave oven protects its user with metal walls and a metal grid in the door. Explain how this works and name the harm it prevents.
questions.modelAnswer: The metal surfaces reflect and contain the microwaves so they cannot escape the cavity, preventing the internal heating of body tissue that excessive microwave exposure would cause.
